investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing all four required contract assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState, orgId, agentId). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely] Node pool for remote agents has not scaled out — only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and neither has been replaced or augmented with additional capacity, so any concurrent or residual agent workload exhausts the pool.
[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user sessions are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and were not cleaned up, reducing available capacity to zero.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec restrict scheduling to a labeled subset of nodes that currently has zero schedulable capacity, compounding the resource exhaustion.

[Lower likelihood] A node maintenance event, cordon, or taint applied to the 2 kata-capable nodes reduced their effective allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm count to zero around the time of the eval run.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written — causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod VM required to back a remote agent. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144s before the eval timed out. Because agent creation never completed, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 (createAgent call) never returned an agent object, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never populated, producing a complete contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: the cluster has only 2 nodes that carry the kata peer-pod VM resource, and both reported insufficient capacity at the time of the eval run. All three remote-agent checks attempted to schedule pods concurrently or in close succession, competing for the same scarce resource.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, leaving no fallback nodes even if VM slots were available elsewhere.

Tertiary — no preemption victims available: the scheduler found no lower-priority pods on the 2 kata-capable nodes that could be evicted to free a VM slot, indicating those nodes were already fully utilized by running workloads.

Lower confidence — transient cluster scaling lag: the cluster may not have auto-scaled to add additional kata-capable nodes before the eval timeout window elapsed (warningLatencyMs=240000, outageLatencyMs=360000 per source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-184), though the eval failed well within those thresholds at ~151s.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing all four required contract assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState, orgId, agentId). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely] Node pool for remote agents has not scaled out — only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and neither has been replaced or augmented with additional capacity, so any concurrent or residual agent workload exhausts the pool.
[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user sessions are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and were not cleaned up, reducing available capacity to zero.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec restrict scheduling to a labeled subset of nodes that currently has zero schedulable capacity, compounding the resource exhaustion.

[Lower likelihood] A node maintenance event, cordon, or taint applied to the 2 kata-capable nodes reduced their effective allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm count to zero around the time of the eval run.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned a live agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written — causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod VM required to back a remote agent. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144s before the eval timed out. Because agent creation never completed, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 (createAgent call) never returned an agent object, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never populated, producing a complete contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), the exhaustion was transient and has since resolved — not a persistent capacity problem.

If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two eligible nodes was not fully consumed at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling or quota issue should be investigated.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod matches all 6 nodes (i.e., the 4-node exclusion is a recent regression), the root cause would shift to a node labeling or affinity configuration change rather than capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a concurrent run, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a cluster-wide scheduling constraint.

If the failure message changes to a different error (e.g., API authentication, network timeout) on re-run, the scheduling error was a one-time transient event unrelated to sustained capacity exhaustion.
